recommendations.wine_name: Chablis Premier Cru Montée de Tonnerre
recommendations.reasoning: Delivers the laser acidity and mineral-driven whites you consistently reach for. Montée de Tonnerre is the purest expression of Chablis flint and oyster shell — untouched by oak, exactly aligned with your avoided-oak preference.
recommendations.confidence: high — chardonnay top varietal, Chablis top region, zero oak
recommendations.nose: Flint, oyster shell, and lemon zest with a chalky mineral spine.
recommendations.palate: Lean, precise, and mouthwateringly acidic with a long saline finish.

recommendations.reasoning: Unlike the oaky, tropical whites you avoid, this Loire Sauvignon Blanc delivers cut-grass and grapefruit intensity with linear acidity. Pairs beautifully with tonight's seafood without competing.
recommendations.confidence: high — sauvignon blanc varietal match, Loire region overlap
recommendations.nose: Grapefruit, cut grass, and flint with a lifted white-flower note.
recommendations.palate: Crisp and linear with vibrant acidity and a clean, citrus-inflected finish.

recommendations.wine_name: Muscadet Sèvre et Maine sur Lie
recommendations.reasoning: An underrated value that punches above its price with the same mineral-saline character you prize in Chablis. Extended lees contact adds a yeasty complexity without sacrificing acidity.
recommendations.confidence: medium — style alignment strong, varietal (Melon de Bourgogne) is adjacent rather than a top pick
recommendations.nose: Lemon curd, sea salt, and yeast with a subtle almond note.
recommendations.palate: Light-bodied with zesty acidity, a creamy lees texture, and a clean saline finish.

list_quality_note: A thoughtfully curated French-white-focused list with excellent Loire and Burgundy representation.
profile_match_summary: All three picks align with the profile's preference for mineral-driven, high-acidity whites with zero or negligible oak — precisely the counterpoint to the avoided oaky-whites style.
